source: Hong, Kottimukkalur & Noh (2026) 'Uncertain Text and Price Reactions to Earnings Releases', Journal of Banking & Finance vol. 182
title: H350 stub: Text Uncertainty Anti-Filter for H174 PEAD Entries
rationale: Hong et al. (JBF 2026) find that firms with higher text uncertainty in 10-K/Q filings exhibit stronger immediate price reactions to earnings surprises but WEAKER post-earnings announcement drifts. This is directly actionable for our H174 PEAD strategy: high-uncertainty firms are bad PEAD candidates because the market immediately processes the surprise with little delay. Key mechanism: text uncertainty attracts sophisticated institutional attention, which accelerates price discovery and eliminates the PEAD drift that H174 exploits. Implementation: compute Loughran-McDonald uncertainty word count / total words from the 8-K filing, threshold TBD (median split or top tercile). Hypothesis: filtering OUT high-uncertainty firms from H174 entries should raise the win rate above 81.8% by removing entries where drift will be weak. This directly extends H174 (score>=0.18 + surprise>=0.02) with a third filter: LM_uncertainty < threshold. Data: Loughran-McDonald master dictionary available free (www.loughranmcdonald.com); EDGAR 8-K text already downloaded in PEAD pipeline. Cost of implementation: ~1 day (add uncertainty parser to pead_overnight.py, backtest on historical H174 events). Risk: may reduce n below 20-event OOS gate (currently n=22 OOS).
implementation_notes: Compute: lm_uncertainty_ratio = count(LM_uncertainty_words in 8-K text) / total_word_count
Filter gate: only enter PEAD trade if lm_uncertainty_ratio < median(historical 8-K uncertainty ratios)
Backtest: apply filter retroactively to all historical H174 events (n=22 OOS) and check if WR improves
Expected sample reduction: ~25-30% (top half uncertainty excluded) → n_oos ~15-16, may violate n>=20 gate
Alternative: use tercile split instead of median to keep more events
